skill.name: systematic-debugging
skill.description: Four-phase root cause investigation before attempting fixes. Use when debugging bugs, test failures, or unexpected behavior.
skill.summary: Guides root cause debugging through investigation, pattern analysis, hypothesis testing, and focused implementation.
skill.author: DMJGilbert

content.user_title: Debug Software with Root Cause Discipline
content.value_statement: Bugs often waste time when teams patch symptoms before they understand the cause. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through evidence-based debugging phases.
actual_capabilities: Prompts root cause investigation before any proposed fix.
Directs users to reproduce failures and read complete error messages.
Encourages comparison with working code before implementation.
Structures debugging around explicit hypotheses and one-variable tests.
Requires verification after the fix and a return to investigation when needed.
limitations: It provides a reasoning workflow, not an automated debugger.
It depends on available errors, tests, logs, and repository context.
It does not guarantee the resolution rates stated in the source text.
It may need domain knowledge for complex architecture decisions.

use_cases.title: Investigate Test Failures
use_cases.description: Guide a developer from failing output to a verified root cause before changing code.

use_cases.title: Review Production Regressions
use_cases.description: Help an engineering lead compare recent changes with stable behavior and isolate likely causes.

use_cases.title: Coach Debugging Practice
use_cases.description: Teach junior contributors to gather evidence, form hypotheses, and avoid repeated random fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Failing Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me debug this failing test. Use the four phases and start by asking for reproduction steps and the full error message.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Unexpected Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: I have unexpected behavior in a feature. Guide me through evidence gathering, data flow tracing, and a single hypothesis test.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this regression with me. Compare recent changes with a working path, list differences, and identify the most likely root cause.

prompt_templates.title: Reset After Failed Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: We tried three fixes and the issue remains. Stop further patching, reassess the architecture, and propose a focused investigation plan.

output_examples.input: A test started failing after a dependency upgrade.
output_examples.output: The assistant requests exact failure text and reproduction steps. It compares recent dependency changes with working behavior. It proposes one tested hypothesis before any fix.

output_examples.input: A feature returns inconsistent results in one environment.
output_examples.output: The assistant traces data flow from the observed error. It asks for boundary evidence and checks configuration differences before implementation.

output_examples.input: Several patches did not solve the same defect.
output_examples.output: The assistant stops further patching. It returns to root cause investigation and questions whether the current design pattern is sound.

best_practices: Capture exact errors, reproduction steps, and recent changes before proposing a fix.
Compare broken behavior with a working implementation before editing code.
Test one hypothesis at a time and verify the result before continuing.
anti_patterns: Applying quick patches before proving the root cause.
Changing multiple variables in one debugging attempt.
Continuing to patch after repeated failed fixes without re-investigation.

faq.question: What problems is this skill designed for?
faq.answer: It is for bugs, test failures, regressions, and unexpected runtime behavior where the cause is not proven.

faq.question: Does it run diagnostics automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a reasoning workflow. The AI tool may still need permission to inspect files or run tests.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It works well with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when they can inspect errors, tests, and recent changes.

faq.question: When should I invoke it?
faq.answer: Use it when a fix is uncertain, repeated fixes failed, or the same issue returns.

faq.question: Does it require test-driven development?
faq.answer: It emphasizes a failing test before implementation when the project supports tests.

faq.question: Are the success rate claims guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. The percentages in the source are motivational claims, not measured guarantees for every project.
